title: Custom Hook Examples
description: Explore practical custom Git hooks for protecting branches, auto-generating changelogs, and enforcing team conventions.

data.text: Custom hooks can automate almost any aspect of your Git workflow. This lesson provides practical examples: protecting main from direct pushes, auto-formatting files on commit, generating changelog entries, and enforcing branch naming conventions.
The pre-push hook can check if the target branch is main or another protected branch and reject the push if it comes from an unauthorized source.

data.title: Pre-push: block direct pushes to main
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/pre-push

PROTECTED_BRANCHES="main master production"

while read local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
  # Extract branch name from refs/heads/<branch>
  BRANCH=$(basename "$local_ref")
  TARGET_BRANCH=$(basename "$remote_ref")
  
  # Check if pushing to a protected branch
  if echo "$PROTECTED_BRANCHES" | grep -qw "$TARGET_BRANCH"; then
    if [ "$BRANCH" = "$TARGET_BRANCH" ]; then
      echo "Direct push to $TARGET_BRANCH is not allowed."
      echo "Use a pull request instead."
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
done

exit 0

data.title: Server-side hooks are more reliable
data.text: Client-side pre-push hooks can be bypassed with --no-verify. For critical protection, implement the same logic as a server-side pre-receive hook on your Git server.
Instead of asking developers to run a formatter before committing, have the pre-commit hook format staged files automatically. This ensures consistent formatting regardless of developer setup.

data.title: Pre-commit: auto-format staged files
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/pre-commit

STAGED_FILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM)

if [ -z "$STAGED_FILES" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Format C# files
CS_FILES=$(echo "$STAGED_FILES" | grep '\\.cs$')
if [ -n "$CS_FILES" ]; then
  echo "Formatting C# files..."
  echo "$CS_FILES" | xargs dotnet format --include
  echo "$CS_FILES" | xargs git add
fi

# Format JSON files
JSON_FILES=$(echo "$STAGED_FILES" | grep '\\.json$')
if [ -n "$JSON_FILES" ]; then
  echo "Formatting JSON files..."
  echo "$JSON_FILES" | xargs prettier --write
  echo "$JSON_FILES" | xargs git add
fi

echo "Formatting complete."
exit 0

data.text: The post-commit hook can append the commit message to a CHANGELOG.md file automatically. This keeps the changelog up to date without requiring manual maintenance.

data.title: Post-commit: append to CHANGELOG
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/post-commit

COMMIT_HASH=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
COMMIT_MSG=$(git log -1 --format=%B "$COMMIT_HASH")
COMMIT_AUTHOR=$(git log -1 --format='%an' "$COMMIT_HASH")
DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)

CHANGELOG="CHANGELOG.md"

# Append to Unreleased section if it exists
if grep -q '^## \[Unreleased\]' "$CHANGELOG"; then
  sed -i "/^## \[Unreleased\]/a \n- $COMMIT_MSG ($COMMIT_AUTHOR, $DATE)" "$CHANGELOG"
  echo "Changelog updated."
else
  sed -i '1i ## [Unreleased]\n\n- \"$COMMIT_MSG\" ('\"$COMMIT_AUTHOR\"', '\"$DATE\"')\n' "$CHANGELOG"
  echo "Changelog created."
fi

exit 0

data.text: The pre-commit hook can verify the current branch name follows your team's naming convention before allowing a commit. This prevents badly named branches from entering the team's workflow.

data.title: Pre-commit: enforce branch naming
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/pre-commit

BRANCH=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null)

# Allowed prefixes: feature/, fix/, hotfix/, chore/
if ! echo "$BRANCH" | grep -qE '^(feature|fix|hotfix|chore)/[A-Z]+-[0-9]+'; then
  echo ""
  echo "Branch name does not follow convention: $BRANCH"
  echo "Expected format: <type>/<TICKET-ID>-<description>"
  echo "Examples:"
  echo "  feature/AUTH-123-add-login"
  echo "  fix/AUTH-456-token-expiry"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

echo "Branch name valid: $BRANCH"
exit 0

data.text: The post-checkout hook can automatically install dependencies or sync environment files when switching branches. This is useful for projects where different branches require different dependency versions.

data.title: Post-checkout: install dependencies on branch switch
data.code:
#!/bin/bash
# .git/hooks/post-checkout

PREV_BRANCH=$1
NEW_BRANCH=$2
IS_BRANCH_SWITCH=$3

# Only run on branch switches, not file checkouts
if [ "$IS_BRANCH_SWITCH" = "1" ]; then
  echo "Switched to branch: $NEW_BRANCH"
  
  # Install dependencies if package.json changed
  if git diff --name-only "$PREV_BRANCH" "$NEW_BRANCH" | grep -q '^package.json$'; then
    echo "package.json changed — installing dependencies..."
    npm install
  fi
fi

exit 0

items.question: How do I share custom hooks with my team?
items.answer: Use Husky to commit the hook scripts to your repository. The .husky/ directory is tracked in Git and installed automatically when teammates run npm install.

items.question: Can hooks interact with external services?
items.answer: Yes. Pre-push hooks can trigger CI pipelines, post-commit hooks can post to Slack, and pre-commit hooks can call external APIs for validation.

items.question: What if my hook depends on a tool that is not installed?
items.answer: Check for the tool at the start of the hook and provide a clear error message. For Node.js tools, verify with command -v before running.

items.question: Are there performance considerations for complex hooks?
items.answer: Yes. Cache results where possible, run checks in parallel, and avoid network calls in pre-commit hooks. Move expensive operations to CI or pre-push.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Protect branches by checking branch names in pre-push or pre-commit
Auto-format staged files in pre-commit for consistent code style
Use post-commit to append changelog entries automatically
Use post-checkout to sync environment when switching branches
Share hooks with Husky so the entire team uses the same automation
